prospects.headline_long: Fresh off a $350M round at a ~$7.5B valuation on more than $600M of ARR, AlphaSense - the AI market-intelligence platform for the financial world - is a pre-IPO leader with no motorsport footprint, and no research-intelligence brand owns the F1 grid.
prospects.the_case: AlphaSense is the AI platform for market intelligence and search across the financial and business world - the tool banks, asset managers, hedge funds and a majority of the S&P 500 use to find and trust insight. On 3 June 2026 it closed a $350M round at a ~$7.5B valuation (led by Vitruvian Partners, Accenture Ventures and J.P. Morgan Growth Equity Partners), nearly doubling its 2024 mark, on more than $600M of ARR. It has scale and momentum - the $930M Tegus acquisition in July 2024 folded in the leading expert-transcript library - and CEO Jack Kokko has said an IPO is a possibility. Two things make it a 1440 target: it has never touched motorsport, and no market- or financial-intelligence brand owns a position anywhere on the F1 grid, so the category is uncontested. Its audience - research, strategy and investment professionals - is exactly the premium enterprise crowd an F1 partnership reaches.
prospects.why_now: A $350M raise at a doubled, ~$7.5B valuation is the peak moment of brand-investment authority, and CEO Jack Kokko's openness to an IPO puts AlphaSense in the pre-listing window when enterprise credibility compounds most. A CMO appointed in 2024 with two IPO runs behind her is setting the brand agenda now. The market-intelligence category on the grid is empty and cheap to lock before a data or research rival notices the same open lane.
prospects.why_team: McLaren is the sharpest canvas: a premium, technology-forward team with the deepest enterprise-B2B partner roster on the grid - Dell, Salesforce, Workday and Google among them - which means a proven hospitality machine pointed at exactly the corporate decision-makers AlphaSense sells to. The market-intelligence category is uncontested there, so AlphaSense can own it outright. If McLaren's inventory is constrained, Williams (a data-led revival with a B2B-tech audience) and Aston Martin (boardroom-premium) are credible fallbacks.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE B - a real off-car value exchange. AlphaSense's market and competitive intelligence serves a team's commercial and strategy functions directly: sponsor and partner prospecting, category and market analysis, and tracking the businesses a team wants in its garage. McLaren gains a genuine intelligence capability plus co-marketing to a shared enterprise audience; AlphaSense gains a premium global stage and hospitality in front of the finance and corporate buyers it sells to. The honest framing is a commercial and brand partnership, not an in-car technical integration.
prospects.deal_architecture: Official Market Intelligence Partner tier on McLaren, minimum three years, estimated $3-5M/yr, with category exclusivity for market/financial intelligence and research, B2B hospitality aimed at AlphaSense's finance and corporate-strategy buyers, and digital/content rights for its enterprise audience. Williams or Aston Martin are the documented fallbacks.

prospects.name: JFrog
prospects.thesis: The CMO who ran marketing at Udemy during its multi-series McLaren partnership now owns the brand budget at JFrog ($531.8M revenue, +24%, FCF-positive) - and the software-supply-chain-security slot on the F1 grid is still empty. A warm, proven motorsport buyer pointed at a clean category.

score_rationale.timing: CMO Genefa Murphy appointed Jan 5 2026 for a declared 'next growth phase'; FY2027 brand-budget planning is forming now, and a new CMO's first marquee investments are typically locked within the first two quarters.
score_rationale.capacity: FY2025 revenue $531.8M (+24%), cloud $243.3M (+45%), $142.3M FCF, NDR 119%, 74 customers above $1M ARR. A $3-5M/yr deal is roughly 0.1% of revenue - immaterial to the balance sheet.
score_rationale.brand_fit: No software-supply-chain-security brand is anywhere on the F1 grid (Confluent = data streaming on Williams). JFrog can OWN the category outright, and Murphy's public thesis - 'trust, control and discipline at velocity' - is almost a motorsport tagline already.
score_rationale.urgency: Direct rivals Sonatype and Snyk are circling the same whitespace; whoever signs first locks category exclusivity for three years and forces the others onto rival teams.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE A: an F1 team ships thousands of software builds a season across simulation, strategy and car systems - that is a literal software supply chain, so JFrog earns a genuine in-garage technical-partner role, not a sticker.

prospects.headline_long: The CMO who ran marketing at Udemy during its multi-series McLaren partnership now runs marketing at JFrog - a profitable, cash-generative public company - and the software-supply-chain-security slot on the F1 grid is still completely empty.
prospects.the_case: On 5 January 2026 JFrog appointed Genefa Murphy as Chief Marketing Officer for what it explicitly framed as its 'next growth phase' in AI-driven software supply chain management. Murphy is the decisive signal in this brief: as Chief Marketing & Content Officer at Udemy she led marketing through its multi-series McLaren Racing partnership (Formula 1, IndyCar, NEOM McLaren Formula E and Extreme E). She is therefore not a cold prospect who must be educated on the value of motorsport - she has been inside exactly this kind of programme - and she now controls the brand budget of a company with $531.8M revenue (+24% YoY), $243.3M cloud revenue (+45%) and $142.3M of free cash flow. The strategic gap is just as compelling as the relationship: while Confluent (data streaming) sits on the Williams livery, no software-supply-chain-security brand exists anywhere on the F1 grid. JFrog's category - the integrity and security of the code that ships software - is the single largest piece of uncontested enterprise whitespace in the paddock, and Murphy's own positioning language maps onto F1 almost word-for-word.
prospects.why_now: Three clocks are running simultaneously. First, Murphy is roughly five months into a mandate her own company has branded a growth-phase reset - the precise window in which a new CMO defines the multi-year brand-investment agenda and shapes the next fiscal year's budget, before priorities harden. Second, because she has already delivered an F1/FE programme, the usual internal objection - 'does motorsport actually work for a B2B audience?' - is pre-answered by her personal track record, collapsing the normal 12-18 month education cycle to near zero. Third, the category whitespace is a depreciating asset: the moment a DevSecOps rival (Sonatype, Snyk or GitLab) plants a flag, JFrog's first-mover narrative is gone and the conversation becomes a defensive one. Moving in the next 4-6 weeks captures all three.
prospects.why_team: McLaren is the warm, high-probability path. Murphy already knows the McLaren commercial organisation intimately from negotiating and activating the Udemy partnership, so an introduction is a re-engagement rather than a cold pitch, and McLaren's technology-forward, precision-engineering brand identity is the closest cultural mirror on the grid to JFrog's 'secure software, shipped fast' promise. If McLaren's relevant inventory is constrained, Aston Martin is the strong fallback: it carries premium enterprise gravitas, its hospitality audience skews to exactly the CISO and CTO buyers JFrog sells to, and its technology-partner roster leaves the DevSecOps slot open. Either team lets JFrog tell a 'from first commit to chequered flag' supply-chain-integrity story in front of the right room.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A - a genuine two-way technical partnership, not branding alone. A modern F1 team operates a sprawling internal software estate: aerodynamic and strategy simulation, real-time race-systems code, telemetry pipelines and hundreds of engineers shipping builds every week. That is, by definition, a software supply chain - and securing and managing it is exactly what JFrog's platform does (artifact management, binary lifecycle, security scanning across the dev pipeline). A deal can therefore be structured around a real integration into the team's engineering workflow, giving McLaren an authentic 'official software supply chain partner' story it can stand behind technically, plus a credible R&D narrative, plus enterprise hospitality where JFrog's own buyers already gather on race weekends. The team gains tooling and a reference customer; JFrog gains a live proof point and a stage.
prospects.deal_architecture: Recommended entry: Official Software Supply Chain Partner tier on McLaren (Aston Martin as fallback). MINIMUM THREE YEARS at an estimated $3-5M/yr, calibrated to JFrog's $531.8M revenue base. Scope: car and driver-suit branding in the software-supply-chain-security category, garage and B2B hospitality access, digital and content inventory aimed at an enterprise-IT audience, a working technical integration into the team's dev pipeline, and - critically - a category-exclusivity clause that blocks any DevSecOps rival from the team for the life of the contract.

prospects.headline_long: Nvidia-backed Cohesity reached ~$1.5B pro-forma ARR (revenue $1.7B+) after completing its Veritas combination in Dec 2024 and is steering toward a 2026 IPO benchmarked against public peer Rubrik (~$14.5B today) - with no pure-play backup and data-resilience brand yet owning the F1 grid.
prospects.the_case: Cohesity is the rare combination our mandate prizes most: an established category leader arriving at a brand-reckoning moment with budget, motive and a clear strategic angle. After completing its combination with Veritas' data-protection business on 10 December 2024, the merged company reported pro-forma annual recurring revenue of roughly $1.5 billion (revenue over $1.7 billion) at a 28% adjusted cash-EBITDA margin, and the Nvidia-backed company is now steering toward a 2026 IPO with a valuation its CEO has benchmarked against publicly traded peer Rubrik (a ~$14.5B market cap as of May 2026; the Sep-2025 CNBC report that framed the comparison cited Rubrik at ~$17B). Two things make it a 1440 target rather than just a big company. First, it has never touched motorsport, so an approach now is early - we would not be the hundredth agency in the inbox. Second, no pure-play enterprise backup, recovery and ransomware-resilience brand yet owns a presence on the F1 grid, and the cleanest way to own it is Cadillac - the American team debuting in 2026 whose verified tech roster (IFS for ERP, TWG for AI) carries no data-protection or cybersecurity partner. As the grid's American flag-bearer, Cadillac also aligns Cohesity's brand with the US institutional investors its IPO roadshow must win. The IPO is the forcing function that turns 'someday' into 'this year'.
prospects.why_now: An IPO is the single largest brand-elevation event in a company's life, and the 12 months around it are when leadership spends most deliberately on institutional credibility - exactly the currency a multi-year F1 partnership trades in. Signing around the listing lets Cohesity convert a finance milestone into a global enterprise-brand statement, pre-build the recognition that public investors reward, and secure backup-and-resilience category exclusivity before a direct rival (Rubrik, Veeam, Commvault) claims the same adjacent lane. The post-Veritas integration narrative also benefits from a single, high-visibility external proof point that the merged company is now one coherent market leader.
prospects.why_team: Cadillac is the sharpest canvas for this brand at this moment. It debuts in 2026 with a greenfield tech roster - IFS runs ERP, TWG provides AI, but no partner owns data protection, backup or cybersecurity - so Cohesity can be a FOUNDING partner and own the data-resilience category rather than share it. It compounds strategically: Cadillac is the grid's American flag-bearer and Cohesity is a US company heading into a US-market IPO, so the partnership speaks straight to the institutional investors the roadshow must win, with hospitality at the US rounds. The trade-off: a first-year team's media value is unproven - Williams is the documented fallback for a more established, data-led audience.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A - a real operational fit. A brand-new team stands up its entire race and factory data estate - telemetry, simulation, design IP - from zero, and protecting and recovering it is mission-critical from day one. That is Cohesity's domain: backup, rapid recovery and ransomware resilience, complementing IFS (ERP) rather than competing. Cadillac gains real resilience and a 'we protect the data that builds a winning team' story; Cohesity gains a high-visibility American launch partner to name on the IPO roadshow.
prospects.deal_architecture: Founding Data Resilience Partner of the Cadillac F1 Team. MINIMUM THREE YEARS - ideally four, to span the IPO and the post-listing brand-build cycle - at an estimated $4-7M/yr (debut-team entry pricing should favour an early founding partner). Scope: garage and car branding in the backup-and-recovery category, hospitality at the US rounds targeting enterprise-IT and investor audiences, digital rights, a working data-protection deployment for the new team, and exclusivity scoped to backup/recovery/ransomware-resilience. Williams is the documented alternative if a more established, data-led audience is preferred.

Second, the company has just expanded its leadership - a new CEO in Rajeeb (Raj) Hazra and a new CMO in Lawrence Schwartz - which is exactly the configuration that approves first-mover brand investments to establish a public-market identity. prospects.name: Mistral AI

score_rationale.timing: Fresh mega-round funding a global enterprise brand-build and a 'European AI sovereignty' narrative.
score_rationale.brand_fit: Europe's AI champion fits a European-rooted, sustainability-led championship.
score_rationale.urgency: AI brands are racing for enterprise mindshare; an FE presence differentiates, but no dated trigger.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE A: AI for strategy and data analysis is a credible team use case.

prospects.headline_long: Europe's frontier-AI champion Mistral is flush with capital and brand ambition - and Formula E is the European, sustainability-native stage it has never used, with no AI lab yet holding an FE team deal.
prospects.the_case: Mistral AI, freshly capitalised at a multi-billion valuation, is building a global enterprise brand and a 'European AI sovereignty' narrative that resonates strongly with European institutions and enterprises. Formula E - European-rooted, sustainability-led and internationally broadcast - is a natural stage for that story, and no frontier-AI lab currently holds a Formula E team partnership, leaving the category open. For a company defining itself as Europe's answer in AI, an association with the world's premier electric racing championship is an unusually on-message brand and talent platform. Note the slightly higher crowding (~70): Mistral is well known and already courted, so the angle must be sharply differentiated by team fit and a real technical workstream.
prospects.why_now: Post-raise brand budgets, an enterprise-mindshare land-grab among AI labs, and an uncontested FE category make a multi-year platform attractive now. The differentiator is speed and specificity: with crowding rising, the team-fit and technical-substance pitch must arrive before Mistral commits its brand attention elsewhere.
prospects.why_team: Nissan pairs a global EV pioneer's Formula E pedigree with an international, technology-forward identity. A French AI champion on a globally-recognised EV team tells a clean 'European innovation, global stage' story; if a French-team option re-emerges as the grid settles post-DS, it can be revisited, but Nissan offers the strongest combination of pedigree and reach today.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A. AI-driven race strategy, energy-management modelling for an all-electric powertrain, and large-scale data analysis are real FE problems where Mistral's models could be deployed as a working technical partnership. Nissan gains a genuine AI collaboration and innovation narrative; Mistral gains a live, referenceable deployment and a sustainability-aligned brand stage.
prospects.deal_architecture: Official AI / Technology Partner tier on Nissan Formula E, minimum three years, ~$3-5M/yr, with AI-category exclusivity and a defined data/strategy activation workstream.

score_rationale.timing: Took first external capital (March 2025, $600M) and appointed a first President (Colin Murdoch) - early in its brand life, low urgency.

prospects.headline_long: DeepMind spin-out Isomorphic Labs raised $600M into unicorn territory and named its first President - a British AI deep-tech with a precision-science story, low inbound crowding, and no motorsport footprint, ideal to court early.
prospects.the_case: Isomorphic Labs, the DeepMind/Alphabet spin-out applying AI to drug discovery, took its first external capital ($600M) in 2025, entering unicorn territory, and has begun building out its leadership (appointing Colin Murdoch, who also serves as Google DeepMind's Chief Business Officer, as its first President). The standout attribute is low inbound crowding (~25): almost no one in motorsport has called them, so 1440 could be early by a wide margin. It is a British, precision-science brand whose talent-attraction and credibility goals could be served by a measured, tasteful Formula E association - a long-horizon relationship to build now, before the company scales its brand spend and the crowd arrives.
prospects.why_now: This is a relationship-first play, not a deal to force this quarter. The value of acting now is positional: getting in while crowding is near zero and a newly-formed commercial leadership is open to ideas, so that when Isomorphic does turn to brand and talent marketing, 1440 is already the trusted motorsport partner rather than one of fifty inbound pitches.
prospects.why_team: Jaguar TCS Racing - British, premium, technology-and-sustainability-led - is the natural cultural and geographic fit for a London deep-tech brand, and its blue-chip audience suits a science-led company focused on credibility and recruitment over consumer reach.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE B. This is primarily a science, innovation and talent-brand association rather than an in-car technical integration; the value sits in a shared 'precision and discovery' narrative and a recruiting halo for both organisations. Kept deliberately modest and optional-to-scale, it gives Jaguar a distinctive, prestige-science partner and Isomorphic a tasteful, high-credibility brand stage - with room to deepen only if both sides see value.
prospects.deal_architecture: Start with a modest Official Partner tier on Jaguar TCS Racing, minimum three years, ~$2-3M/yr, structured to grow, with emphasis on talent/employer-brand activation rather than heavy consumer signage.

prospects.ticker: Private (a16z, Microsoft, Silver Lake Waterman, Sixth Street, Capital One Ventures)

score_rationale.timing: President Molly Matthews appointed May 12 2026 alongside CCO and CPO promotions; the leadership honeymoon window is open but narrowing.

score_rationale.urgency: Confluent - a direct iPaaS rival - is on the Williams 2026 livery, and the association hardens every race weekend.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE A: integration/automation tooling has a credible team-systems use.

prospects.headline_long: SnapLogic appointed a President and expanded its C-suite the same day, while direct rival Confluent sits on the Williams livery - SnapLogic cannot cede the enterprise-credibility stage to a competitor.
prospects.the_case: On 12 May 2026 SnapLogic appointed Molly Matthews (ex-Microsoft enterprise GTM) as President while simultaneously promoting its Chief Customer Officer and Chief People Officer - a deliberate scale-up posture carrying new budget authority and appetite for brand investment. Backed by a16z, Microsoft, Silver Lake Waterman, Sixth Street and Capital One Ventures, with $100M+ ARR confirmed in August 2025 and customers including AstraZeneca, Adobe, Verizon and Sony, the company has both the means and the motive. The decisive competitive signal: Confluent, a direct iPaaS rival, is an active partner on the Williams 2026 livery, putting a competitor on motorsport's enterprise-credibility stage in front of the exact CTO and CDO audience SnapLogic needs.
prospects.why_now: Matthews's appointment created a leadership window in which new Presidents routinely approve first-mover brand investments to establish a GTM identity, and that window narrows by the week. Simultaneously, Confluent's Williams presence hardens with every race weekend, so a rival-team announcement now reframes the narrative before the competitor's association solidifies - the urgency is genuinely time-boxed.
prospects.why_team: Aston Martin (with McLaren as an alternative) places SnapLogic directly opposite Confluent's Williams partnership - turning a competitor's sponsorship into SnapLogic's own urgency argument and landing the brand in front of the same enterprise IT decision-makers. Aston Martin's premium gravitas and open integration category make it the cleanest counter-position.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A. Integration and automation tooling maps to a team's sprawling systems estate - sponsor and commercial data, logistics, and telemetry pipelines that must talk to each other - so SnapLogic can support a real technical-partner narrative and a working integration rather than a logo, while the team gains genuine connectivity tooling.
prospects.deal_architecture: Associate / Official Partner tier on Aston Martin (or McLaren): garage access, digital inventory and B2B hospitality. MINIMUM THREE YEARS - re-architected up from the original two-year proposal in Brief N 009 - at ~$3-5M/yr, calibrated to $100M+ ARR, with integration-category exclusivity.
